classification.difficultyReason: Calculate disjoint Venn regions from overlapping totals, then use these counts to find three probabilities.

content.prompt: In a group of 50 students, 30 study mathematics, 25 study physics and 20 study both.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Represent this information on a Venn diagram.

answer.short: Let $M$ represent mathematics and $P$ represent physics. Mathematics only: 10; both: 20; physics only: 5; neither: 15.
answer.worked:
Let $M$ represent students studying mathematics and $P$ represent students studying physics. Place 20 in the intersection.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Mathematics only}&=30-20=10\\\text{Physics only}&=25-20=5\\\text{Neither}&=50-(10+20+5)=15\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: One student is selected at random from the group. What is the probability that the student studies:

answer.worked:
There are $30-20=10$ students who study mathematics but not physics.

$$\begin{align*}P(\text{mathematics but not physics})&=\frac{10}{50}\\P(\text{mathematics but not physics})&=\frac15\end{align*}$$

There are $25-20=5$ students who study physics but not mathematics.

$$\begin{align*}P(\text{physics but not mathematics})&=\frac{5}{50}\\P(\text{physics but not mathematics})&=\frac1{10}\end{align*}$$

The Venn diagram gives $50-(10+20+5)=15$ students who study neither subject.

$$\begin{align*}P(\text{neither subject})&=\frac{15}{50}\\P(\text{neither subject})&=\frac3{10}\end{align*}$$
